accepted.question_text: For the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d, does there exist an absolute integer constant c such that every strong orientation of Q_d contains a directed cycle of length at most c? In other words, can one bound the length of the shortest directed cycle in every strongly connected orientation of every hypercube by a constant independent of d?

evidence.quote: Does There exist an integer c such that for every d ∈ N, every strong orientation of Qd, the hypercube of dimension d, has a directed cycle of lenght ≤ c ?

accepted.question_text: Given a tournament T, an integer k, and vertices x and y of T, must T contain two arc-disjoint spanning branchings: an in-arborescence rooted at x and an out-arborescence rooted at y, with each branching having at most k leaves? Equivalently, characterize or decide when a tournament admits arc-disjoint in- and out-branchings with prescribed roots and with both branchings having at most k leaves.

evidence.quote: given T a tournament, k an integer, x and y vertices of T, does T contain arc-disjoint in- and out-arborescences with roots x and y and both with at most k leaves ?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a graph. Form the inversion graph L(G) whose vertices are all orientations of G, and where two orientations are adjacent when one can be obtained from the other by choosing a set X of vertices and reversing every arc whose two ends both lie in X. What is the diameter of L(G)? In particular, is it always true that diam(L(G)) ≤ Δ(G), where Δ(G) is the maximum degree of G?

evidence.quote: For a digraph D and a subset X of vertices of D, the inversion of X, is the digraph obtained from D by inversing all the the arcs of D with both ends in X.
From a graph G, link two orientations of G if you can pass from one to the other by the inversion of a set. Build like that the inversion graph L (G) of G on all the orientations of G.
What is the diameter of L (G) ? Do we have diam(L (G)) ≤ ∆(G) ?

accepted.question_text: Fix a class of tournaments of bounded clique-width. Is there a constant number of colors and a CMSO-definable binary formula φ(x, y) such that, for every tournament T in the class, one can choose a coloring λ of the vertices so that φ interprets a total order on V(T), meaning that for all vertices x and y, x < y holds in that order exactly when the colored structure (T, λ) satisfies φ(x, y)?
accepted.context_brief: Logical definability of orders in tournaments

evidence.quote: There exists c, and φ logical formula, such that for all tournament T there exists a total order on the vertices, a coloring λ such that x < y iff T,λ satifies φ(x, y).
Does it work for a class of tournaments with bounded clique-width and CMSO logic ?

accepted.question_text: More generally, can one represent a total order on the vertices of an arbitrary tournament by first coloring the vertices and then using a first-order formula with modulo-counting predicates to define the relation x < y? That is, does there exist such a definability scheme for all tournaments in FOL plus modulo counting?
accepted.context_brief: FOL with modulo counting on tournaments

evidence.quote: There exists c, and φ logical formula, such that for all tournament T there exists a total order on the vertices, a coloring λ such that x < y iff T,λ satifies φ(x, y).
In general, with FOL + modulo counting ?

accepted.question_text: For a digraph D and a vertex ordering L, call a directed path forward in L if its vertices appear in the same order as the orientation of the path. What is the smallest integer k such that every digraph D admits k vertex orderings L_1, ..., L_k with the property that for every two distinct vertices v_i and v_j, either some ordering L_ℓ contains a forward path from v_i to v_j or some ordering L_ℓ contains a forward path from v_j to v_i?
accepted.context_brief: Forward paths across multiple vertex orderings

evidence.quote: Question : What is the minimal k such that for every digraph D there exists enumerations L1, . . . , Lk with for every vi ̸= vj ∈ V(D) either there is a forward path from vi to vj in some Ll or there is a forward path from vj to vi in some Ll .

accepted.question_text: Is the problem of computing directed pathwidth fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the width? Equivalently, although an XP algorithm is known for directed pathwidth on general digraphs, does there exist an FPT algorithm for this parameterized problem?

evidence.quote: There exists an XP algorithm to compute the directed pathwidth for the digraphs in general. It is open to know if an FPT algorithm exists or not (but probably not).

accepted.question_text: Let C be the class of digraphs generated by the following rules: the oriented graph K_2 belongs to C; adding a twin of a vertex of a graph in C keeps the graph in C; and gluing two members of C along at most two non-adjacent vertices again produces a member of C. Does every digraph in C have bounded dichromatic number, or can the dichromatic number in this class grow arbitrarily large?
accepted.context_brief: Dichromatic number of a recursively built class

evidence.quote: Build C a class of digraphs as follow : oriented K2 is in C , adding a twin to a vertex of a graph of C results in a graph of C and the graph obtained from two members of C glued on at most 2 non-adjacent vertices is a member of C .
Does the defined class have bounded dichromatic number ?

accepted.question_text: Given a digraph D, can its arc set always be partitioned into two linear forests, where a linear forest means a disjoint union of directed paths?

evidence.quote: A linear forest is the union of directed paths.
Algorithmic question : can we partition the arcs of a diraph D into two linear forests ?

accepted.question_text: Given a digraph D, can its arc set be partitioned into two linear forests in such a way that the connected components of one of the two forests all have bounded length?

evidence.quote: Same question with bounded length for the components of one of the linear forest ?

accepted.question_text: If D is restricted to be an orientation of a cubic graph, can the arcs of D be partitioned into two linear forests?

evidence.quote: What about if D is the orientation of a cubic graph

accepted.question_text: Does every digraph D of maximum out-degree k contain an in-dominating set X such that the chromatic number of the underlying undirected graph induced by X is at most log k? Here, an in-dominating set means a set X such that every vertex outside X has at least one out-neighbor in X.
accepted.context_brief: In-dominating sets with small chromatic number

evidence.quote: An in-dominating set X of a digraph D is a subset of vertices of D such that every vertex not in X has at least one out-neigbour in X.
Does every digraph D with maximal out-degree k admit an in-dominating set X with χ(D[X]) ≤ log k (where χ is the usual chromatic number of the underlying graph) ?

accepted.question_text: Given a 3-uniform hypergraph H, decide whether there exists a digraph D such that the hypergraph H_D on V(D), whose hyperedges are exactly the induced directed cycles of D, is equal to H.
accepted.context_brief: Recognizing hypergraphs of induced directed cycles

evidence.quote: From a digraph D = (V,A), build the hypergraph HD on V whose hyperedges are the induced directed cycles of D.
Given a (3-uniform) hypergraph H , decide if there exist D such that HD = H .

accepted.question_text: Let C be the class of undirected graphs generated by the rules that K_1 and K_2 belong to C, and gluing two graphs from C along at most two non-adjacent vertices again yields a graph in C. Can one construct a graph in C whose chromatic number is 4?
accepted.context_brief: Chromatic number of a glued graph class

evidence.quote: Build C a class of (undirected) graph as follow : K1 and K2 are in C , and a graph obtained from two members of C glued on at most 2 non-adjacent vertices is a member of C . Can you build a graph of C with chromatic number 4 ?

accepted.question_text: Is every triangle-free graph with no 3-connected subgraph 3-colorable?

evidence.quote: Addendum : Is it true that every graph that contains no triangle and no 3-connected subgraph is 3-colorable ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a function f such that every tournament T with dichromatic number χ⃗(T) at least f(k) contains two disjoint vertex sets A and B such that A dominates B and both induced subtournaments satisfy χ⃗(A) ≥ k and χ⃗(B) ≥ k?
accepted.context_brief: Highly colorable tournaments with a dominating split

evidence.quote: There exists a function f such that for every tournament T with −→χ (T) ≥ f (k) contains two disjoint sets of vertices A and B such that A dominates B and −→χ (A) ≥ k and −→χ (B) ≥ k.

accepted.question_text: Under the same high-dichromatic-number hypothesis on a tournament T, can one weaken one side of the conclusion by asking only that one of the two disjoint sets has dichromatic number at least k while the other has minimum out-degree and minimum in-degree both at least k? More precisely, must there exist disjoint sets A and B with A dominating B such that either χ⃗(A) ≥ k and min{δ⁺(B), δ⁻(B)} ≥ k, or the symmetric converse condition holds?
accepted.context_brief: Semi-degree variant of the tournament split conjecture

evidence.quote: What about if we ask for −→χ (A) ≥ k and min{δ+(B),δ−(B)} ≥ k or the converse ?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Can we ask the same for the mad of the digraph ?

evidence.quote: Can we ask the same for the mad of the digraph ?

evidence.quote: What are the digraphs D such that HD is critical (in sens of the hyperedges) ?
